name: uniwire
description: Draw and check electrical single-line and multi-line diagrams from a plain description.

interface.longDescription:
uniwire turns a plain description of an electrical installation into a single-line or multi-line diagram that has been checked against electrical rules.

Describe a home, a shop, an office or a workshop (supply, main breaker, residual-current devices, circuits, loads) and uniwire builds the document, validates it, checks it against the rule profiles of NF C 15-100 (France) and IEC 60364 (protection ratings against cable cross-sections, 30 mA protection, circuits per RCD, dedicated circuits, selectivity...) and returns two links: one opens the drawing in the uniwire web editor, the other downloads the PDF drawn by uniwire. It can also edit an existing diagram (add a circuit, change a rating), list wires and wire markers, and produce a bill of materials.

Who it is for: electricians, electrical design offices, students and anyone preparing a panel layout.

Limitations: the checks are automatic checks of the data in the document, not a conformity certificate; a qualified electrician must verify any installation before it is built. Very large installations (more than 1,500 elements) are refused. Documents are kept 30 days so that the links work; do not include personal data.

uniwire is an open standard and open-source software (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/uniwire-dev/uniwire
capabilities: Draw single-line and multi-line electrical diagrams
Check installations against NF C 15-100 and IEC 60364 rules
Give a link to the drawing and a PDF download
Edit a diagram: add circuits, change ratings
Wire lists, wire markers and bills of materials
defaultPrompt: Draw the single-line diagram of a 60 m2 flat, single-phase, TT earthing, and check it.
Draw the panel of a small bakery in three-phase 400 V and give me the PDF.
Check this panel: is a 32 A breaker fine for the oven on a 4 mm2 cable?

positive.description: Draw and check a small flat
positive.prompt: Draw the single-line diagram of a 60 m2 flat: single-phase 230 V, TT earthing, lighting, sockets, a washing machine and an oven. Check it.
positive.expected_behavior: Builds a uniwire document, reports the check result (errors and warnings) and gives a link that opens the drawing in the uniwire web editor plus a PDF link.

positive.prompt: Draw the panel of a small bakery in three-phase 400 V: 12 kW oven, 3 kW dough mixer, cold room, lighting, sockets and a till. Give me the PDF.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a checked diagram with three-phase and single-phase circuits and a pdf_url link that downloads the PDF drawn by uniwire.

positive.prompt: Check this circuit: a 32 A breaker feeding sockets on a 1.5 mm2 copper cable, in a French dwelling.
positive.expected_behavior: Reports the NF C 15-100 cross-section finding (1.5 mm2 is limited to 16 A) and proposes a fix such as a 16 A breaker or a 6 mm2 cable.

positive.prompt: Start from the example studio apartment, add a 7 kW EV charger on its own circuit and check the result.
positive.expected_behavior: Adds the EV charging circuit with its protection, reports the check result and gives the updated links.

positive.prompt: Give me the wire marker list for the example factory motor control centre.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the wire marker rows (one per wire end) of the example, as a table.

negative.prompt: What is the weather in Paris tomorrow?
Design a 3D bracket for a shelf and export it as STEP.
Tell me how to replace a breaker in my panel while it is powered.

review.commerce_description: uniwire is free; it does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: First release: draw, check (NF C 15-100, IEC 60364), edit and export electrical single-line and multi-line diagrams, with links to the web editor and the PDF.
